Do you work in an English-speaking business environment and feel shy when communicating? This lesson will help you build confidence and improve your communication skills in a professional setting. Through engaging conversations and role-playing, you will practise a variety of essential business communication skills.

What we will cover:
Focus on Confidence Building:
    - Gain the ability to communicate your ideas clearly and effectively in the workplace.

Interactive Practice:
    - Conversations on various business topics using written and audio content.

Speaking & Vocabulary Development:
    - Practise reading out loud.
    - Learn industry-specific terminology.
    - Discuss relevant business topics to improve fluency.

Role-Playing Exercises:
    - Mock meetings.
    - Interviews.
    - Practise sessions for real-world professional situations.

These exercises will help you speak more comfortably in meetings, presentations, and other professional scenarios.

teacher_info.intro: I enjoy talking with people from all over the world, and I have a keen interest in current event news. I keep myself up to date on international news stories, and I use this knowledge in my interactions with my students.
teacher_info.short_signature: I am a fully qualified CELTA English Teacher. I have 7 years teaching experience.
teacher_info.introduction: I graduated form high school in Dublin in 1983, I then went on in 2014 to study teaching with CELTA in International House in Bangkok. I have spent the last 3 years teaching to Thai; Kinder Garten, Primary, and Secondary students. I also have held private lessons for young adults. For the younger learners I use activities to help engage the students, I also use media in the form of Videos. I use a projector to supplement my lessons. For older learners I use role play, and a variety of activities, in conjunction with media. Some of the topics that I use in my lessons include. . . 'What happens next?' I show the students a video, and the video is paused just before the end. The students are split up into three teams of 10, and they compete as teams to guess What happens next? from 3 possible outcomes. This type of lesson is exciting, and entertaining. 'The Quick Brown Fox!' This is a game that is suitable for any grade of student. The sentence 'THE QUICK BROWN FOX JUMPS OVER THE LAZY DOG' is written on the whiteboard. Each student is given the opportunity to recite the alphabet in sequence from A-Z by pointing a pointer at each letter. They are given a time limit of 30 seconds. When the time is up a buzzer sounds. This is a great ice breaker, and it gives the students confidence. 'Let's go shopping' By using a combination of Flash Cards, and media, i teach the students new vocabulary. The vocabulary will include general everyday nouns that we use when shopping for clothes. I then split the students into pairs. I give one student a Flashcard with a picture of a 'shirt' for example. I give the other student play money. Then the students are asked to role play 'shopping for a shirt'. This activity promotes conversation, and develops the student's use of vocabulary. I have experience in teaching beginners, intermediate, and advanced learners. I approach the lesson from the learner's point of view, and structure the lesson to meet the learner's requirements.

teacher_info.about_teacher: As a teacher, I prioritize my own patience and comprehension. It's crucial to my students' learning that I see past mistakes enough to accomplish a certain level of communication, meanwhile noticing the patterns and frequency of those errors to better understand how to correct them. I like to have fun with my students, and that means letting down my own wall a bit so that we both feel like we know the person who we're speaking with. Comfort is crucial in learning just as comprehension is crucial in teaching.
teacher_info.teaching_style: The first session with me is typically free of lesson plans and study points. No matter the student's level of English, it's important to establish a fluid communication as a basis for the future of our classes. While we get to know each other, I am quietly taking notes on the student's habits in speaking English as well as their areas of interest to use as a focus for lesson plans. We will exercise all four areas of language: speaking, reading, writing and listening, but always with a heavier focus on speaking. As the classes progress we rotate through these areas while constantly adding vocabulary and grammar rules, as I help the student to fix their habits from the root of the mistakes.

pro_course_detail.title: Confidence and Social Skills
pro_course_detail.description: Through my years of teaching I’ve noticed that when advanced students still struggle with English integration, they find that the problem is rooted in their confidence in social situations. Speaking in your second or third language comes with added worries about cultural or syntactical differences. I have a set of exercises and discussion topics which will allow us to dig deeper into these nuanced moments of communication, with the goal of adding to your skill set a level of comfort with carrying on a dialogue in any setting. We will discuss your personal perspective and I will offer you options for how to best express yourself.
